Observed: T1 was a fresh 120,000-requested-step PPO run (120,832 actual after rollout rounding), seed 42, under unchanged source commit 95e92976dddec5715a678cde36263ee0b19dcf8e and baseline parameters. The preserved training trajectory rose from zero success proxy through 40,960 steps, reached 0.96 around 79,872, then fluctuated mostly 0.94–0.97 through 120,832; 110,592 was the first archived late-plateau checkpoint and the terminal proxy was not better. This proxy came from the 14–20 cm training sampler, not the official distribution. M1 measured two checkpoints from this same run: T1:checkpoint-110592 scored 181/200 (90.5%) task-reference and 172/200 (86%) on the research panel; T1:checkpoint-120832 scored 171/200 (85.5%) and 168/200 (84%). The panels use different seeds/semantics and their aggregate rates should not be interpreted as a direct evaluator comparison. On the paired research panel, the four discordant episodes all favored checkpoint-110592; this is a modest difference between these artifacts, not a general training-time effect or mechanism. In M1's research diagnostics, checkpoint-110592 had 28 failures: 21 never sampled within tolerance and all 21 targets were 6.1–11.4 cm; seven reached but did not complete the uninterrupted 100-step hold. Checkpoint-120832 had 32 failures: 23 no-reach cases, all 6.1–11.4 cm, and nine post-reach hold failures. Many other inner-radius episodes succeeded; no-reach cases also cluster in some angular sectors (mostly negative-angle sectors in the inspected rows, with exceptions), so radius alone does not explain failure. Several successful/reaching episodes reached within roughly 5–20 control steps, which weighs against universal slow escape from reset as the dominant cause but does not rule out angle-conditioned acquisition difficulty. Diagnostics are sampled at control steps and contain no joint, torque, or within-step traces. Task-reference failure rows are also predominantly at inner radii, with some larger-radius failures, but that fixed panel is not the same seed panel as the research diagnostics.

Interpretation updated against pi_workspace/scientific_model.md: Its kinematic consequence remains unrevised: both elbow-sign IK branches are joint-limit feasible throughout the official region, so these behavioral failures do not establish geometric impossibility. This keeps the decision on learned acquisition/trajectory/hold, not workspace expansion; branch-specific residuals, limit margins, and trajectories would revise that view if they contradicted the calculated feasible solutions. The fully extended reset is rank deficient and every target begins outside tolerance, so leaving the reset can matter; however, early observed reaches mean the present evidence does not justify making generic singularity escape the lead explanation. If inner no-reach cases remain after broader training coverage, target-conditioned joint/end-point traces and branch errors from reset would redirect work toward reset/IK-branch control. The direct bounded motor commands are held across ten physics substeps and there is no authored position servo: reaching is not holding. M1's seven and nine post-reach failures make stabilization a real competing limitation; if the new candidate reaches inner targets but still loses the hold, full error/velocity/command traces through hold and maximum-hold/interruptions would support a stabilization direction. The model's compiled inertia/contact response remains unknown and could change approach/braking conclusions, but neither panel identifies it; posture-conditioned torque response, inertias and contact counts would matter if traces show path- or posture-specific dynamic failures. The observation omits hold progress and episode time, which could make task state partially observed, but no current result attributes failure to that omission; matched physical states with different hold histories/horizons and saved-runtime decisions would be needed before changing the observation or policy memory. Because this is one recipe and one seed, either result is limited to that implementation and would not prove or disprove broader coverage methods. If coverage does not change the decision, branch-conditioned joint/endpoint trajectories and torque response are the next physical discriminator; compiled dynamics and within-step hold details remain open but are not required to prioritize the first comparison.

pi_checkpoint.current_synthesis:
Observed: T1 was a fresh 120,000-requested-step PPO run (120,832 actual after rollout rounding), seed 42, under unchanged source commit 95e92976dddec5715a678cde36263ee0b19dcf8e and baseline parameters. The preserved training trajectory rose from zero success proxy through 40,960 steps, reached 0.96 around 79,872, then fluctuated mostly 0.94–0.97 through 120,832; 110,592 was the first archived late-plateau checkpoint and the terminal proxy was not better. This proxy came from the 14–20 cm training sampler, not the official distribution. M1 measured two checkpoints from this same run: T1:checkpoint-110592 scored 181/200 (90.5%) task-reference and 172/200 (86%) on the research panel; T1:checkpoint-120832 scored 171/200 (85.5%) and 168/200 (84%). The panels use different seeds/semantics and their aggregate rates should not be interpreted as a direct evaluator comparison. On the paired research panel, the four discordant episodes all favored checkpoint-110592; this is a modest difference between these artifacts, not a general training-time effect or mechanism. In M1's research diagnostics, checkpoint-110592 had 28 failures: 21 never sampled within tolerance and all 21 targets were 6.1–11.4 cm; seven reached but did not complete the uninterrupted 100-step hold. Checkpoint-120832 had 32 failures: 23 no-reach cases, all 6.1–11.4 cm, and nine post-reach hold failures. Many other inner-radius episodes succeeded; no-reach cases also cluster in some angular sectors (mostly negative-angle sectors in the inspected rows, with exceptions), so radius alone does not explain failure. Several successful/reaching episodes reached within roughly 5–20 control steps, which weighs against universal slow escape from reset as the dominant cause but does not rule out angle-conditioned acquisition difficulty. Diagnostics are sampled at control steps and contain no joint, torque, or within-step traces. Task-reference failure rows are also predominantly at inner radii, with some larger-radius failures, but that fixed panel is not the same seed panel as the research diagnostics.

Interpretation updated against pi_workspace/scientific_model.md: Its kinematic consequence remains unrevised: both elbow-sign IK branches are joint-limit feasible throughout the official region, so these behavioral failures do not establish geometric impossibility. This keeps the decision on learned acquisition/trajectory/hold, not workspace expansion; branch-specific residuals, limit margins, and trajectories would revise that view if they contradicted the calculated feasible solutions. The fully extended reset is rank deficient and every target begins outside tolerance, so leaving the reset can matter; however, early observed reaches mean the present evidence does not justify making generic singularity escape the lead explanation. If inner no-reach cases remain after broader training coverage, target-conditioned joint/end-point traces and branch errors from reset would redirect work toward reset/IK-branch control. The direct bounded motor commands are held across ten physics substeps and there is no authored position servo: reaching is not holding. M1's seven and nine post-reach failures make stabilization a real competing limitation; if the new candidate reaches inner targets but still loses the hold, full error/velocity/command traces through hold and maximum-hold/interruptions would support a stabilization direction. The model's compiled inertia/contact response remains unknown and could change approach/braking conclusions, but neither panel identifies it; posture-conditioned torque response, inertias and contact counts would matter if traces show path- or posture-specific dynamic failures. The observation omits hold progress and episode time, which could make task state partially observed, but no current result attributes failure to that omission; matched physical states with different hold histories/horizons and saved-runtime decisions would be needed before changing the observation or policy memory. Protected within-control-step occupancy is also unresolved: the public diagnostics sample after a control interval and cannot establish substep excursions. The official 100-step contract remains authoritative; protected trajectory evidence or the final assessment would revise claims about actual official behavior, and no development panel certifies it.

The baseline training environment has a single 14–20 cm sampler constant, while the official uniform-radius range is 6–20 cm; thus 8/14 (4/7, about 57%) of official radial probability is omitted and more-folded postures are required. This is evidence for a consequential coverage test, not proof of cause: inner-radius successes, angle clustering, and post-reach failures are counterevidence to a radius-only account. The proposed 6–20 cm run would retain the PPO architecture, parameters, reward, observation, runtime, task mechanics, seed and budget, changing only training exposure. Improvement concentrated among inner-radius complete-episode outcomes would support coverage as a contributor in this recipe; unchanged angle-conditioned no-reach would redirect toward acquisition/branch control; successful reaching with interrupted holds would direct work toward stabilization. One fresh seed cannot establish a general result about all coverage methods, and a null result would not disprove that broader method. There is no completed result from I1 yet.
pi_checkpoint.decision_frontier: The campaign must choose between a terminal assessment of a candidate with 90.5% task-reference and 86% research-panel performance, or bounded work with a credible prospect of changing the candidate before that assessment. The immediate scientific distinction is whether exposing PPO to the missing official inner radii materially improves complete-episode success, or whether the repeated angle-conditioned no-reach and post-reach hold failures remain. I1 will compare a fresh full-budget, seed-42 run changing only the sampler lower bound (14 to 6 cm) against T1:checkpoint-110592 on the same fixed task-reference panel and the same paired research episode seeds, using success and radius/angle-stratified first reach, maximum hold and interruptions. Inner-radius gains would support further coverage development; no meaningful gain with persistent angular no-reach would favor reset/branch/trajectory evidence; reaching without uninterrupted holds would prioritize stabilization. This is recipe- and seed-specific. Compiled dynamics/contact, omitted hold/time state, and protected substep semantics remain uncertainties with specified discriminators above, but current aggregate and control-step evidence does not make them more decision-relevant than the sampler comparison. If the planned training or measurement fails or lacks those diagnostics, the distinction remains unresolved rather than counting as a negative scientific result.
